title: Memory SSA: version the memory, then walk for the clobber (§2 example)
summary_caption: Def/Use/φ chains give memory a use-def graph: one cheap walk proves nothing in the loop clobbers %p3 — the fact LICM needs.

frames.caption: The note's worked example: a store to %p3 above the loop, a store diamond inside it. Memory SSA will give every memory op a version.
entry: the store to %p3 may write memory, so it becomes MemoryDef 1 — its input is liveOnEntry, the state on function entry.
while.cond merges entry with the loop back edge, so it gets MemoryPhi 6 = φ(1, ?). The back-edge input isn't known yet.
if.then: the store to %p1 is MemoryDef 2. Its input is 6 — the memory version reaching this block.
if.else: the store to %p2 is MemoryDef 3, also fed by 6. Each arm now produces its own memory version.
if.end joins the two arms, so another merge: MemoryPhi 5 = φ(2, 3) — whichever store actually ran.
load %p1 only reads: MemoryUse(5). It stops at φ 5 because one incoming def — 2, the store to %p1 — really can clobber it.

set_labels.end:
if.end
5 = φ(2, 3)
Use(5): load %p1
store %p2
load %p3

frames.caption: The store to %p2 becomes MemoryDef 4, chained after 5 — every def records the version it may overwrite.

set_labels.end:
if.end
5 = φ(2, 3)
Use(5): load %p1
4 = Def(5): store %p2
load %p3

frames.caption: Version 4 flows around the back edge and completes MemoryPhi 6 = φ(1, 4). The chains are built — one use is left.
Naively load %p3 would be MemoryUse(4), its nearest def. But uses get optimized: 4 writes %p2, which never aliases %p3 — walk past it.

set_labels.end:
if.end
5 = φ(2, 3)
Use(5): load %p1
4 = Def(5): store %p2
Use(4): load %p3

frames.caption: The walk climbs through φ 5 into both arms: defs 2 and 3 write %p1 and %p2 — no alias with %p3 either. Keep climbing, through φ 6.
Behind φ 6, def 1 is the store to %p3 itself — and the clobber on every path. The load is optimized to MemoryUse(1).

set_labels.end:
if.end
5 = φ(2, 3)
Use(5): load %p1
4 = Def(5): store %p2
Use(1): load %p3
